Summary

Enhance the date range banner on /support/analytics to display timestamps formatted in the user's local timezone (e.g., 2026-09-08 07:00 to 2026-10-07 10:15 (WIB)), reflecting real-time data up to the last fetch timestamp.

Problem Statement

Currently, the telemetry banner displays raw date strings without time (Range: 2026-09-08 to 2026-10-07).
Because Countly tracks metrics in near real-time and dates in the API represent UTC boundaries:

  • Support agents cannot easily see whether "today's" data covers the entire day or is a live cut-off up to the current moment.
  • Support agents cannot easily correlate UTC boundaries with their actual working business hours in local time.

Scope of Changes

  • In src/pages/Support/Analytics/Analytics.jsx:
    • Format start_date (00:00:00 UTC) into local browser datetime (YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm).
    • Format end_date:
      • If end_date is today, format up to the live fetched_at timestamp.
      • If end_date is a past date, format up to end of day (23:59:59 UTC).
    • Include the local timezone code/offset (e.g. (WIB) / (GMT+7)).
    • Gracefully fallback to plain dates if timestamps are unavailable.
  • In src/pages/Support/Analytics/Analytics.test.jsx:
    • Add test cases verifying local datetime range rendering.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Range displays full date and time in the user's local browser timezone.
  • For current day ranges, the end time reflects the real-time fetched_at cut-off.
  • Local timezone is indicated alongside the range.
  • All unit tests pass with 100% assertions.

issues.display_title: Issue #4388: feat(auth): make Single Sign-On (Keycloak) the login method via a feature switch
issues.main_description_html:
Background

Single Sign-On (SSO) login through Keycloak is currently hidden. It can only be reached by adding a special parameter to the login page address, which is not something regular users can do. We want to switch SSO on or off for everyone through a single setting in the dashboard instead.

Goal

Add one on/off switch for SSO login:

  • On: the login page takes users straight to the SSO login page. The regular email/password and Google login are not shown.
  • Off: the login page works exactly as it does today.

Scope

  • Login page: follows the switch instead of the special address parameter.
  • SSO error page: "Try Again" takes users straight back to the SSO login page. The "Back to Standard Login" option is removed.
  • When SSO cannot start (for example, SSO is not set up), users see a clear error message with a "Try Again" button instead of the page reloading endlessly.

Out of Scope

  • The Register and Forgot Password pages stay reachable by direct link.

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: With the switch off, the login page shows the regular login form, and the old special address no longer opens SSO.
  • AC-002: With the switch on, opening the login page goes straight to the SSO login page. The regular login form never appears.
  • AC-003: When SSO login fails, "Try Again with SSO" goes straight to the SSO login page.
  • AC-004: If SSO cannot start, users see an error message and a "Try Again" button. The page does not get stuck reloading or showing repeated pop-ups.
  • AC-005: Unit tests cover AC-001 – AC-004.

Related

  • #4259: hidden SSO login entry point
  • #4290: SSO login security update

Result

Implementation

  • PR: #4389 — merged into development on 2026-10-15 (merge commit 1a5a885)
  • Key commit: cd7ee24 — feat(auth): toggle Keycloak SSO via REACT_APP_KEYCLOAK_AUTH_ENABLED env flag
  • Behavior:
    • SSO is switched on/off with the REACT_APP_KEYCLOAK_AUTH_ENABLED setting (off by default). The old ?auth=keycloak address no longer does anything.
    • With SSO on, the login page, "Try Again with SSO" and logout all go straight to the SSO login page. The regular login form is never shown.
    • If SSO cannot start, users see an error message with a "Try Again" button instead of an endless reload.
    • Logout now always ends the SSO session, including on dev and localhost. Before this, users were logged straight back in.
  • Maintenance mode is also controlled by a setting now (REACT_APP_MAINTENANCE_MODE, off by default).
  • To turn SSO on: set REACT_APP_KEYCLOAK_AUTH_ENABLED=true and rebuild the dashboard.

Testing

  • CI=true npx craco test --watchAll=false src/components/Header src/pages/Auth src/pages/Error src/utils/keycloakAuth.test.js → 7 suites, 46/46 passed
    • Switch off → regular login form, old address ignored (AC-001)
    • Switch on → straight to SSO, login form never rendered (AC-002)
    • SSO error → "Try Again with SSO" goes straight to the SSO login (AC-003)
    • SSO not configured / cannot start → error screen + "Try Again", tried once only (no loop) (AC-004)
    • Logout → SSO login page when on, logout API called on localhost too

issues.main_description_html:
Background

There was no written guide for deploying gothru-dashboard. How the build runs on builder-server, where the REACT_APP_* env comes from and which servers get the build were only known by the people who ran them.

Goal

DevOps can deploy the dashboard, check it, and roll it back by following one document in the repo, with the same structure as the API guide.

Scope

  • docs/DEPLOY.md in English, written for DevOps (same structure as the API's docs/DEPLOY.md).
  • Step 1: releases go development → master, and master is deployed.
  • Step 2: REACT_APP_* env is baked in at build time from /home/jenkins/workspace/<folder>/.env on builder-server (with CRA's env-file priority order).
  • Step 3: notify the team.
  • Step 4: run ansible-playbook ansible-deploy.yml on builder-server (npm install --force + npm run build, then rsync --delete of build/ to dev-live 192.168.1.131, live-1 .179, live-2 .180), check PLAY RECAP.
  • Step 5: check the dashboard loads (hard refresh, console, deep-link refresh).
